name: Face tape / sleep patches for wrinkles
lead: Face tape and sleep patches are adhesive strips or silicone and hydrocolloid-style pads that people stick on the forehead, between the brows, around the eyes or on the mouth area before bed. The aim is a smoother face: users want to flatten or prevent lines that form from facial expression or sleeping position, so they wake looking less creased and keep skin looking younger over time. They are sold as cosmetic products rather than medical devices with a recognised wrinkle indication.

Wikipedia lists habitual facial expressions and habitual sleeping positions among the causes of wrinkles, alongside ageing, sun damage, smoking and poor hydration [1]. Established treatments are different in kind: botulinum toxin, which is FDA-approved for glabellar (frown) lines, injectable fillers, and the prescription retinoids tretinoin and tazarotene, the only topical retinoids approved for photodamage-related wrinkles [1]. The Wikipedia wrinkle article does not mention tape or patches [1].

No published clinical trials of face tape or sleep patches for wrinkles were located in the sources reviewed for this article. Claims about them rest mainly on manufacturer marketing and user testimonials.
infobox: Overnight, on forehead, brows, eyes or mouth area

paras: Products include thin flexible tape cut into strips, silicone sheets reusable across several nights, and hydrocolloid or hydrogel patches that sit on the skin. Some carry added ingredients such as peptides or hyaluronic acid, which fall into the glycosaminoglycan and hydration-product category that Wikipedia describes as offering temporary support for hydration.[1]

Wrinkles are attributed to habitual expressions, sleeping positions, sun damage, smoking, ageing, glycation, loss of body mass and poor hydration [1]. Retinol and similar over-the-counter products have some supporting evidence but are regulated as cosmetics, hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxylapatite are the most common dermal fillers, botulinum toxin products immobilise the muscles that cause lines, and ablative lasers remove thin skin layers and are described as more effective than non-ablative ones [1]. Topical glycosaminoglycan products offer temporary relief [1].

Proponents say that keeping the skin physically held flat limits creasing from repeated expression or from pressing the face into a pillow, and that occlusion keeps the area moist. Habitual sleeping position is listed among recognised contributors to wrinkles.[1] Occlusive films in general are known to slow water loss from skin.[2] Whether tape alters wrinkle depth over time has not been tested in a published trial.

Hydrocolloid dressings, the material family some patches borrow from, are self-adhesive pads with a gel-forming layer that creates a moist environment under the dressing; they are used on superficial wounds and as small patches for acne, and a similar sealed, moist environment is the idea behind some wrinkle patches [3].

Adhesives can cause contact dermatitis or irritation in some users; moisturisers and skin-contact products in general are documented causes of contact dermatitis.[2] Dermatologists commonly caution that sensitive or broken skin may react to adhesives, but no study specific to these products was identified.

card.summary: Overnight forehead and brow stickers promising to smooth lines in your sleep, with marketing behind them and no trial data.
card.aka: Wrinkle patches, forehead tape, anti-wrinkle sleep tape
card.note: No published trials; adhesives can irritate skin.

quick.overview:
Face tape and sleep patches are stickers worn overnight on areas that crease, such as the forehead, brow or around the eyes. They are marketed as preventing or softening expression and sleep lines.

No clinical studies of them for wrinkles were found. Established wrinkle treatments are different products entirely, such as botulinum toxin and prescription retinoids.
quick.mechanism: The idea is that holding skin flat and occluded overnight reduces creasing from movement and pillow pressure. Occlusion is known to reduce water loss from skin, but an effect on permanent wrinkles has not been tested.
quick.risks: Adhesives can cause irritation or contact dermatitis in some people. They are sold as cosmetics without a wrinkle-treatment approval.

chain: Patch or tape holds skin flat and covered overnight
Less creasing from expression and pillow pressure
Smoother-looking forehead, brow and eye area
angle.text: People wear the strips at night so skin is held smooth while they sleep, aiming for fewer visible expression and sleep lines and a fresher look in the morning. Some products also add hydrating ingredients.
